comment: The Firefox release whose Rust code passed the engine's networking check (check_networking: the Rust library imports no recv, send, gethostby*, getserv* or getproto* function). Written by scripts/build/networking_check.py from a reading of libgkrust.a in a build with the mozconfig.no-lto variant; scripts/release/rehearse_release.sh --precheck runs it. A unit test requires this record to name the release engine.json pins, and release_manifest.py refuses to publish any other. It is a statement by whoever ran the script, reviewed in the pull request that lands it: CI checks that it names the pinned release, not that the build happened. Only the maintainer may pin a release without the check: "result": "accepted" with "accepted_in" naming the issue or pull request where he said so, and "built_with" as `networking_check.py <version> --inputs` prints it.
how: scripts/build/networking_check.py read libgkrust.a of a build with Rust's own link-time optimisation and no cross-language LTO or sanitiser: 267052 symbols, 6874 undefined names; by the engine's rule it imports none of the engine's 21 networking functions.
